podcast.body: This song was inspired by Ian Curtis's own epilepsy and also reportedly by the sight of a woman he knew who suffered from epilepsy and eventually died from a seizure so intense it proved fatal. "Here's a song inspired by both Ian's epilepsy and apparently the sight of a woman he knew who also had epilepsy and eventually suffered a seizure so intense that she died. It's called She's Lost Control."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was written by Ian Curtis after he witnessed a woman suffering an epileptic fit, an experience that mirrored his own struggles with the condition and contributed to the increasingly dark and depressing nature of his lyrics. "She said I was going to go again. Joint division and she's lost control. The song Ian Curtis wrote when he saw a woman fall victim to an epileptic fit, not unlike his own."

podcast.body: This track is from the 1979 album "Unknown Pleasures," an album intentionally released with minimal liner notes to foster a sense of mystery and encourage imaginative listening. "Joy Division from unknown pleasure's from 1979 and she's lost control."
